title: Europe since 1945
tagline: Occupation and division, welfare and the treaties, decolonisation and 1968, 1989, and the arguments that are still open
summary: The last course begins with zones, the Federal Republic and the GDR, NATO and the treaties of Paris and Rome. It treats welfare as several settlements, decolonisation as European history, and 1968 as more than one event. It follows 1989, the end of the USSR, the Yugoslav wars, the euro, enlargement, Brexit, and the invasion of Ukraine as a war that, in 2026, is not over.
overview: Division is made by occupation, currency reform, the Berlin blockade, two German constitutions and a military alliance. The Marshall speech and the Truman Doctrine are context from outside the continent. They are not a sufficient history of European choices.

The ECSC and the EEC are treaties with members and with exclusions. Welfare states differ, and a typology published in 1990 is not a description of 1950. Decolonisation — India and Pakistan, Dien Bien Phu, Algeria, the Portuguese empire — belongs in this course because the empires were European.

1989 is a sequence: Poland, Hungary, the Wall, Prague, Bucharest. The USSR ends in December 1991. The wars in Yugoslavia are part of the same decade. Maastricht, the euro and the enlargements build a union whose membership changes again with Brexit. The full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022 is stated as an invasion still unfinished in 2026, without a casualty total and without a speech for a policy.
outcomes: Date the Berlin blockade, NATO, the Basic Law and the founding of the GDR.
Distinguish the ECSC from the EEC, and give the date of the Treaties of Rome.
Explain why Indian independence and the Algerian war are part of a European history course.
Order the main events of 1989 and the dissolution of the USSR in December 1991.
State the dates of the Maastricht treaty, the 2004 enlargement, Brexit, and the invasion of 24 February 2022, with the limits the chronology requires.

history.title: Two republics and an alliance
history.detail: NATO is signed on 4 April 1949. The Federal Republic’s Basic Law is dated 23 May. The German Democratic Republic is founded on 7 October.

history.title: Rome
history.detail: On 25 March 1957 the Treaties of Rome establish the European Economic Community and Euratom. Membership is small, and several European states are outside it.

history.title: The Wall is opened
history.detail: On 9 November 1989 the Berlin Wall is opened. It is one event in a year that also includes the Polish Round Table and the fall of Ceaușescu.

history.title: An invasion, unfinished
history.detail: On 24 February 2022 Russia begins a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. As of 2026 the war has not ended. This atlas states the fact and does not offer a casualty total or a policy.

references.title: Postwar: A History of Europe Since 1945
references.note: The survey this course argues with: division, prosperity, memory and the eastern half of the continent restored to the narrative.

references.title: Dark Continent: Europe’s Twentieth Century
references.note: A shorter history of the century that refuses to treat democracy as Europe’s default setting.

references.title: To Hell and Back: Europe, 1914–1949
references.note: Closes the war and opens the division. The sequel, Roller-Coaster, carries the later decades.

references.title: Project Europe: A History
references.note: The European Communities as a project with limits, not as the destination of the continent.
